chunks.en: Brown spots with concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern with yellow margin. Fruit gets infected through calyx or stem attachment; brown concentric rings on fruits.
chunks.hi: पीले किनारे वाले भूरे धब्बे, जिनमें निशाने जैसे गोल छल्ले होते हैं। फल डंठल या बाह्यदल (कैलिक्स) की ओर से संक्रमित होता है; फलों पर भूरे गोल छल्ले।

chunks.en: Survives in infected plant debris. Primary spread through infected seed; secondary spread by spores carried by rain and wind. Favoured by warm, humid (24-29 degree C), rainy and wet weather.
chunks.hi: संक्रमित पौधों के अवशेषों में जीवित रहता है। पहला फैलाव संक्रमित बीज से; बाद में बीजाणु बारिश और हवा से फैलते हैं। गर्म, नम (24-29 डिग्री सेल्सियस), बारिश वाला और गीला मौसम अनुकूल है।

chunks.en: Remove and destroy crop debris. Follow crop rotation.
chunks.hi: फसल के अवशेष हटाकर नष्ट करें। फसल चक्र अपनाएं।

chunks.en: Use resistant or tolerant cultivars. Change the nursery bed location every season, eradicate weeds and volunteer tomato plants, fertilize properly. Avoid planting overlapping crops in adjacent area.
chunks.hi: रोग-रोधी या सहनशील किस्में लगाएं। हर मौसम नर्सरी की जगह बदलें, खरपतवार और अपने-आप उगे टमाटर के पौधे हटाएं, सही खाद दें। पास के क्षेत्र में एक के बाद एक चलने वाली फसलें न लगाएं।

chunks.en: Seed treatment: Trichoderma asperellum @ 4 g/kg seeds.
chunks.hi: बीज उपचार: ट्राइकोडर्मा एस्पेरेलम 4 ग्राम प्रति किलो बीज।

chunks.note: Label claim (CIB&RC) for early blight, leaf spot and late blight; 500 litres spray solution per hectare.
Label claim (CIB&RC) for late and early blight, leaf spot and bacterial wilt.
Label claim (CIB&RC) for leaf spot, early and late blight. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.

Other options on the same page: Iprodione 50% WP 600 g/ac, Metiram 70% WG 1.0 kg/ac, Pyraclostrobin 20% WG 200 g/ac, Zineb 75% WP 800 g/ac, Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC 200 ml/ac, Metiram 55% + Pyraclostrobin 5% WG 600 g/ac, Tebuconazole 50% + Trifloxystrobin 25% WG 140 g/ac.
One of 14 options listed for early blight in the NIPHM package (also captan, copper oxychloride, iprodione, mancozeb, pyraclostrobin, zineb, ziram and mixtures).

chunks.en: Water-soaked black lesions on leaves and stems. Lesions expand rapidly and the entire leaf becomes necrotic. White sporulation on leaves. Dark brown lesions on fruit; soft rot and disintegration of fruits.
chunks.hi: पत्तियों और तनों पर पानी से भीगे जैसे काले धब्बे। धब्बे तेज़ी से बढ़ते हैं और पूरी पत्ती मर जाती है। पत्तियों पर सफेद फफूंद। फलों पर गहरे भूरे धब्बे; फल सड़कर गल जाते हैं।

chunks.en: Spreads through tiny air-borne spores and thrives in wet, humid conditions (15-18 degree C, humidity above 90%). In just 4-5 days the infection spreads widely, causing outbreaks.
chunks.hi: हवा में उड़ने वाले बहुत छोटे बीजाणुओं से फैलता है और गीले, नम मौसम (15-18 डिग्री सेल्सियस, 90% से ज़्यादा नमी) में बढ़ता है। सिर्फ 4-5 दिनों में संक्रमण बड़े क्षेत्र में फैल जाता है।

chunks.en: Grow resistant variety/hybrid Arka Abhed F1. Avoid planting tomatoes in the same field every year. Remove infected plant parts. Ensure enough space between plants and stake them. Use black polythene mulch (30 micron). Improve field drainage and avoid overhead irrigation. Plant windbreaks and avoid late sowing in the monsoon season.
chunks.hi: रोग-रोधी किस्म/संकर अर्का अभेद F1 लगाएं। हर साल उसी खेत में टमाटर न लगाएं। संक्रमित हिस्से हटाएं। पौधों के बीच पर्याप्त दूरी रखें और सहारा दें। काली पॉलीथीन मल्च (30 माइक्रॉन) बिछाएं। खेत में जल निकासी सुधारें और ऊपर से सिंचाई न करें। हवा रोकने वाली बाड़ लगाएं और मानसून में देर से बुवाई न करें।

chunks.en: Proper drainage. Crop rotation.
chunks.hi: सही जल निकासी। फसल चक्र।

chunks.en: Soil application of Trichoderma asperellum (viride) @ 1.0 kg/ac.
chunks.hi: मिट्टी में ट्राइकोडर्मा एस्पेरेलम (विरिडी) 1.0 किलो प्रति एकड़ डालें।

chunks.note: Apply 6 times at 6-day intervals along with soil mulching (preventive, before or at first symptoms).
Label claim (CIB&RC) for early blight, leaf spot and late blight.
Other options on the same page: Azoxystrobin 23% SC 200 ml/ac, Mancozeb 35% SC 1000 g/ac, Zineb 75% WP 800 g/ac, Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC 200 ml/ac.
One of the options listed for Alternaria blight and late blight in the NIPHM package. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.

chunks.en: Small, round to irregular spots with grey centre and dark margin on leaves. Spots join and leaves are blighted; complete defoliation. Stems and flowers are also affected.
chunks.hi: पत्तियों पर छोटे, गोल या टेढ़े-मेढ़े धब्बे, बीच में भूरे-सलेटी और किनारे गहरे। धब्बे आपस में मिल जाते हैं और पत्तियां झुलस जाती हैं; सारी पत्तियां गिर सकती हैं। तने और फूल भी प्रभावित होते हैं।

chunks.en: Survives in infected plant debris; spreads by spores through rain splash or wind. Favoured by high humidity.
chunks.hi: संक्रमित पौधों के अवशेषों में जीवित रहता है; बीजाणु बारिश के छींटों या हवा से फैलते हैं। ज़्यादा नमी अनुकूल है।

chunks.en: Removal and destruction of the affected plant parts.
chunks.hi: प्रभावित हिस्सों को हटाकर नष्ट करें।

chunks.en: Seed treatment: Trichoderma asperellum @ 4 g/kg seeds.
chunks.hi: बीज उपचार: ट्राइकोडर्मा एस्पेरेलम 4 ग्राम प्रति किलो बीज।

chunks.note: Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
Label claim (CIB&RC) for leaf spot.

chunks.en: Small, brown, water-soaked, circular spots with yellow halo on leaves; older leaves fall. Small water-soaked spots on green fruit; the centre of the spots becomes irregular, light brown, sunken and scabby.
chunks.hi: पत्तियों पर पीले घेरे वाले छोटे, भूरे, पानी से भीगे जैसे गोल धब्बे; पुरानी पत्तियां गिर जाती हैं। हरे फलों पर छोटे भीगे धब्बे; बाद में धब्बे का बीच हल्का भूरा, धंसा हुआ और खुरदुरा हो जाता है।

chunks.en: Survives in infected debris; primary spread through infected plant debris and seed, secondary spread by rain splash. Favoured by moist weather, splattering rains, high humidity or persistent dew.
chunks.hi: संक्रमित अवशेषों में जीवित रहता है; पहला फैलाव संक्रमित अवशेष और बीज से, बाद में बारिश के छींटों से। नम मौसम, तेज़ बौछारें, ज़्यादा नमी या लगातार ओस अनुकूल हैं।

chunks.en: Use disease-free seed.
chunks.hi: रोग-मुक्त बीज का उपयोग करें।

chunks.en: Before transplanting, dip seedlings first in a bio-control solution (IIHR organic formulation of Pseudomonas fluorescens + Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/litre, or Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/litre) for 10-15 minutes.
chunks.hi: रोपाई से पहले पौध को 10-15 मिनट जैव-नियंत्रक घोल में डुबोएं (IIHR का स्यूडोमोनास फ्लोरेसेंस + ट्राइकोडर्मा हार्ज़ियानम फॉर्मूलेशन 5 ग्राम प्रति लीटर, या ट्राइकोडर्मा विरिडी या स्यूडोमोनास फ्लोरेसेंस 5 ग्राम प्रति लीटर)।

chunks.note: Two sprays: one in the seed bed after the first true leaves, one after transplanting in the main field.

chunks.en: Severe stunting of plants. Downward rolling and crinkling of the leaves; older leaves become leathery and brittle. Shortened internodes and more side branches give a bushy appearance. The virus is spread by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
chunks.hi: पौधे बहुत बौने रह जाते हैं। पत्तियां नीचे की ओर मुड़ और सिकुड़ जाती हैं; पुरानी पत्तियां चमड़े जैसी कड़ी और भुरभुरी हो जाती हैं। गांठों के बीच की दूरी कम होने और ज़्यादा शाखाएं निकलने से पौधा झाड़ीदार दिखता है। यह विषाणु सफेद मक्खी (बेमिसिया टैबेसी) से फैलता है।

chunks.en: Raise the nursery under a net of sufficient mesh size to keep out whiteflies. Select seed from disease-free healthy plants. Remove and destroy infected plants in the nursery; do not transplant infected seedlings. In the field: field sanitation, rogue out affected plants, grow maize or sorghum as a barrier crop around the field, use yellow sticky traps @ 10/acre.
chunks.hi: नर्सरी ऐसी जाली के नीचे तैयार करें जिससे सफेद मक्खी अंदर न आ सके। स्वस्थ पौधों के बीज चुनें। नर्सरी में संक्रमित पौधे हटाकर नष्ट करें; संक्रमित पौध न रोपें। खेत में: सफाई रखें, प्रभावित पौधे उखाड़ें, खेत के चारों ओर मक्का या ज्वार की बाड़ फसल लगाएं, 10 प्रति एकड़ पीले चिपचिपे ट्रैप लगाएं।

chunks.en: Use 100-mesh nylon net on nursery beds to stop whitefly entry and leaf curl transmission. Grow 5-6 rows of sorghum or maize around the tomato field at least 2 months before transplanting as a barrier against whiteflies, thrips and aphids.
chunks.hi: सफेद मक्खी को रोकने के लिए नर्सरी पर 100-मेश नायलॉन जाली लगाएं। रोपाई से कम से कम 2 महीने पहले खेत के चारों ओर ज्वार या मक्का की 5-6 कतारें लगाएं, जो सफेद मक्खी, थ्रिप्स और माहू को रोकती हैं।

chunks.en: Tolerant/resistant varieties for tomato leaf curl virus: Arka Ananya, Kashi Vishesh, Kashi Amrit, COTH 2, TNAU Tomato Hybrid Co3.
chunks.hi: पत्ती मोड़ विषाणु के लिए सहनशील/रोग-रोधी किस्में: अर्का अनन्या, काशी विशेष, काशी अमृत, COTH 2, TNAU टमाटर संकर Co3।

chunks.en: Conserve whitefly parasitoids (Encarsia, Eretmocerus) and predators. Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) 5% or azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract concentrate @ 80 g in 160 l of water/acre.
chunks.hi: सफेद मक्खी के परजीवी (एनकार्सिया, एरेटमोसेरस) और शिकारी कीटों को बचाएं। नीम बीज गिरी का अर्क (NSKE) 5% या एज़ाडिरेक्टिन 5% नीम अर्क 80 ग्राम, 160 लीटर पानी में प्रति एकड़ छिड़कें।

chunks.note: Label claim (CIB&RC) against the whitefly vector. Alternative: Thiamethoxam 25% WP 0.4 g/litre.

chunks.dose: 60-70 ml in 200 l of water/acre, roots dipped for 15 minutes before transplanting
chunks.note: For management of the leaf curl vector.

chunks.en: Aphids (Myzus persicae, Aphis gossypii) are sucking pests of tomato.
chunks.hi: माहू (मायज़स पर्सिकी, एफिस गॉसिपी) टमाटर का रस चूसने वाले कीट हैं।

chunks.en: Install yellow sticky traps @ 4-5/acre. Use nitrogen fertilizer judiciously.
chunks.hi: 4-5 प्रति एकड़ पीले चिपचिपे ट्रैप लगाएं। नाइट्रोजन खाद सोच-समझकर डालें।

chunks.en: Spray azadirachtin 5% W/W neem extract concentrate @ 80 g in 160 l of water/acre. Release first instar larvae of green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) @ 4000/acre. Conserve lady bird beetles and parasitoids such as Aphidius colemani.
chunks.hi: एज़ाडिरेक्टिन 5% नीम अर्क 80 ग्राम, 160 लीटर पानी में प्रति एकड़ छिड़कें। हरी लेसविंग (क्राइसोपर्ला कार्निया) की पहली अवस्था की इल्लियां 4000 प्रति एकड़ छोड़ें। लेडीबर्ड भृंग और एफिडियस जैसे परजीवियों को बचाएं।

chunks.note: Label claim (CIB&RC) for pinworm, leaf miner, aphids, thrips, whitefly and fruit borer.
Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.

chunks.en: Thrips (Thrips tabaci, Frankliniella schultzei) are sucking pests of tomato.
chunks.hi: थ्रिप्स (थ्रिप्स टैबेसी, फ्रैंकलिनिएला शुल्ट्ज़ी) टमाटर का रस चूसने वाले कीट हैं।

chunks.en: Install blue sticky traps @ 10 traps/ha against thrips; locally available empty tins painted blue and coated with grease, vaseline or castor oil can also be used. Grow 5-6 rows of sorghum or maize around the field as a barrier crop.
chunks.hi: थ्रिप्स के लिए 10 प्रति हेक्टेयर नीले चिपचिपे ट्रैप लगाएं; नीले रंग से रंगे और ग्रीस, वैसलीन या अरंडी के तेल से लेपे खाली डिब्बे भी काम आते हैं। खेत के चारों ओर ज्वार या मक्का की 5-6 कतारें बाड़ फसल के रूप में लगाएं।

chunks.en: Spray entomopathogens such as Beauveria bassiana, Lecanicillium lecanii or Metarhizium anisopliae @ 1 x 10^8 cfu/ml against sucking pests. Neem oil (Azadirachtin 5% EC) @ 2 ml/litre is effective against sucking pests.
chunks.hi: रस चूसने वाले कीटों के लिए ब्यूवेरिया बैसियाना, लेकैनिसिलियम लेकैनी या मेटाराइज़ियम एनिसोप्ली (1 x 10^8 cfu/ml) छिड़कें। नीम तेल (एज़ाडिरेक्टिन 5% EC) 2 मिली प्रति लीटर रस चूसने वाले कीटों पर असरदार है।

chunks.note: Label claim (CIB&RC) for pinworm, leaf miner, aphids, thrips, whitefly and fruit borer.

chunks.en: Field sanitation; rogue out affected plants. Plant tall border crops such as maize or sorghum. Spray thoroughly on the underside of the leaves.
chunks.hi: खेत की सफाई; प्रभावित पौधे उखाड़ें। मक्का या ज्वार जैसी ऊंची बाड़ फसलें लगाएं। पत्तियों के निचले हिस्से पर अच्छी तरह छिड़काव करें।

chunks.en: Conserve predators such as predatory mites (Phytoseiulus, Amblyseius), lady bird beetles, lacewings, predatory thrips, anthocorid bugs and hover flies.

chunks.en: Deep summer ploughing exposes larvae and pupae. Field sanitation. Install pheromone traps @ 4-5/acre for monitoring moths (replace lures every 2-3 weeks); one light trap per acre; bird perches @ 20/acre. For cutworms: tillage at least 2 weeks before planting, use well decomposed manure, flood infested fields, and on small areas collect caterpillars from the soil around plants.

chunks.en: Conduct agro-ecosystem analysis (AESA) weekly in the morning, preferably before 9 a.m., and take management decisions based on the pest and natural-enemy counts only.
chunks.hi: हर हफ्ते सुबह, बेहतर हो 9 बजे से पहले, कृषि-पारिस्थितिकी विश्लेषण (AESA) करें और कीटों व मित्र कीटों की गिनती के आधार पर ही प्रबंधन का फैसला लें।

chunks.en: Avoid growing tomato in the same field season after season; rotate with non-host crops such as cereals and legumes, and do not follow tomato with chilli or brinjal. Stake plants and use drip irrigation to reduce leaf wetness. Collect and destroy infected leaves, shoots and fruits. Spray only need-based, label-claim pesticides.
chunks.hi: हर मौसम उसी खेत में टमाटर न लगाएं; अनाज और दलहन जैसी फसलों के साथ फसल चक्र अपनाएं, और टमाटर के बाद मिर्च या बैंगन न लगाएं। पौधों को सहारा दें और ड्रिप सिंचाई करें ताकि पत्तियां कम गीली रहें। संक्रमित पत्तियां, टहनियां और फल इकट्ठा करके नष्ट करें। केवल ज़रूरत पड़ने पर, लेबल पर दर्ज दवा ही छिड़कें।

chunks.en: Conduct agro-ecosystem analysis (AESA) weekly in the morning, preferably before 9 a.m. Do not take any management decision without considering AESA.
chunks.hi: हर हफ्ते सुबह, बेहतर हो 9 बजे से पहले, कृषि-पारिस्थितिकी विश्लेषण (AESA) करें। AESA देखे बिना कोई प्रबंधन फैसला न लें।

chunks.en: Observe the waiting period of every pesticide without fail. Do not apply pesticides during the 7 days before harvest. Do not spray at midday. Spray the underside of the leaves too, especially for mites, whiteflies and Spodoptera. Do not apply chemical pesticides within 7 days of releasing parasitoids.

chunks.en: Often the incidence starts from nursery itself. Hence, remove infected leaves at the time of planting or within a week of transplanting.

chunks.en: Apply neem cake to furrows (open)/beds (polyhouse) @ 250 kg/ha at planting and repeat after 25 days.

chunks.en: Whitefly is a well-known vector, which transmits tomato leaf curl virus. It has piercing and sucking mouthpart and both nymphs and adults feed on lower surface of the leaves causing deformation of young leaves. Whiteflies also excrete honeydew, causing sooty mold.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Whiteflies - description (p. 4)

chunks.en: Use virus resistant hybrids.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Whiteflies - Management (p. 4)

chunks.en: Raise nurseries in seedling trays under nylon nets or polyhouses.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Whiteflies - Management (p. 4)

chunks.note: Spray in nursery at 15 days after sowing.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Whiteflies - Management (p. 4)

chunks.en: Remove the leaf curl infested plants as soon as disease symptoms are expressed. This helps in reducing source of inoculums of the disease.

chunks.note: After transplanting give need-based sprays at 15 days after planting and do not repeat after fruiting stage as this may leave harmful residues in fruits.

chunks.en: Install yellow sticky traps coated with adhesive or sticky glue at crop canopy level for monitoring adult whitefly population.

chunks.en: If the traps indicate the whitefly activity, spray neem seed kernel extract 4% (NSKE) or pongamia or neem oil (8-10 ml/l) or neem soap (10g/l).

chunks.en: Rogue out the virus affected plants as soon as the symptoms are observed.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Whiteflies - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: This is a minor pest under open conditions and assumes severe form under protected cultivation particularly in ill managed playhouses. Eggs are laid in clusters on foliage. Young larvae feed gregariously on leaves. Mature larvae, migrate and cause extensive damage to leaves and fruits. They hide in soil and crop debris during the day time.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Tobacco Caterpillar - description (p. 5)

chunks.en: Collection and destruction of egg masses and gregarious larvae.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Tobacco Caterpillar - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: Spray Spodoptera NPV 250 LE/ha + 1% jaggery along with sticker (0.5 ml/litre) during evenings.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Tobacco Caterpillar - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: Red spider mites thrive under high temperature, dry weather and are more serious under protected conditions. They are generally found on the lower surface of older leaves. However, when the infestation is very high they attack all parts of the plant and are observed in colonies covered by white-silky webs. Adults and nymphs lacerate the leaves causing yellowing and discoloration.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - description (p. 5)

chunks.en: Remove and destroy the affected leaves.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.note: Under open conditions. Spray lower leaves and lower leaf surface thoroughly as mites are generally observed there.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: As an alternative to the chemical acaricides spray neem oil/neem soap/ pongamia soap 1%.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.note: Under polyhouse conditions, need-based, in rotation with plant products like pongamia oil or neem oil (8-10 ml/l) or neem soap (10 g/l).
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.note: Under polyhouse conditions, need-based, in rotation with plant products like pongamia oil or neem oil (8-10 ml/l) or neem soap (10 g/l).
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: When incidence is severe, remove and destroy all severely infected leaves followed by a spray of mixture of an acaricide with botanicals mentioned above.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Red Spider Mites - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: Root-knot nematodes cause root galls on the feeder roots and sometimes affect the entire root system showing heavy galling. This affects the uptake of nutrition and water and the plants show wilting during warmer part of the day. This causes stunted plants with yellow foliage resulting in yield reduction.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - description (p. 5)

chunks.en: Use nematode resistant variety/hybrid if available.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: Follow crop rotation with marigold, wherever possible.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: Seed treatment with bio-pesticides- Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed. Nursery bed treatment with T. harzianum @ 50 g/ sq. m.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: For the management of nematodes in the main field apply 2 tons of farmyard manure enriched with T. harzianum and Paecilomyces lilacinus per acre before planting, along with 100-200 kg of neem or pongamia cake.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - Management (p. 5)

chunks.note: At transplanting. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
chunks.locator: Insect management - Tomato - Root-knot Nematodes - Management (p. 5)

chunks.en: IPM package in tomato under polyhouse: Raise seedlings in protreys in polyhouse. 15 DAS (Days after seed sowing): Spray the plants with Imidacloprid or Thiomethoam. One day before transplanting: Drench the base of seedlings with Imidacloprid or Thiomethoxam.
chunks.locator: IPM package in tomato under polyhouse (p. 6) - flow chart

chunks.en: At transplanting: Apply neem cake 250 kg/ha. 15 DAP (days after planting): Spray the seedlings with Imidacloprid or Thiomethoxam. 25 DAP (days after planting): Apply neem cake 250 kg/ha.
chunks.locator: IPM package in tomato under polyhouse (p. 6) - flow chart

chunks.en: Post flowering and fruiting stage: Monitor for pest like fruit borer, tobacco caterpillar, leaf miner, whitefly and red spider mite. Erect yellow sticky traps to monitor whitefly. Spray NPV according to the pest. Remove leaves severely infected with leaf miner/red spider mite.
chunks.locator: IPM package in tomato under polyhouse (p. 6) - flow chart

chunks.en: Post flowering and fruiting stage: Spray neem seed powder/neem soap for leaf miner. Spray synthetic acaricide/botanical in rotation to control red spider mite, spray systemic insecticide/botanical to control whitefly.
chunks.locator: IPM package in tomato under polyhouse (p. 6) - flow chart

chunks.en: Irregular leaf spots mostly appear from marginal portion of leaves. In many tomato cultivars, symptoms are V shaped and progress towards midrib. These lesions are having prominent yellowing on their outer margin due to host specific toxin produced by the pathogen. Mostly disease appears in vegetative phase of plant growth before flowering.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Alternaria Blight - Symptoms (p. 23)

chunks.en: Field sanitation by plucking the lower leaves and burning of infected crop debris. Summer ploughing to increase the desiccation of pathogen and infected plant parts. Minimize relative humidity in plant canopy for preventing the infection.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Alternaria Blight - Management (p. 23)

chunks.note: Two spray at 8 days interval is effective against the disease but spray must be started soon after infection on floral part.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Alternaria Blight - Management (p. 23)

chunks.en: Blight appears on foliage as light-pale green water soaked dead area. The lesions are wet in morning and dried, shriveled in daylight. It enlarges rapidly until entire leaves are killed and exposing all the fruits for infection.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Symptoms (p. 23)

chunks.en: In moist and cloudy weather a downy white fungus develops near the outer margin of lesion on underside of the leaves. Green and ripe fruit affected by the blight appear as greenish brown and internal tissues become spongy with bad odour.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Symptoms (p. 23)

chunks.en: Crop rotation with non-solanaceous host is essential for effective reduction of inoculum. Healthy seeds should be collected only from disease-free fruits. Always use healthy and certified seeds collected from disease-free area.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Management (pp. 23-24)

chunks.en: Infected crop debris and fruits must be collected from the field and burnt. Staking of plant reduces all phytophthora diseases of tomato.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Management (p. 24)

chunks.note: Preventive sprays provide good control in cloudy, cold and drizzling weather but spray interval should be 5 to 7 days. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Management (p. 24)

chunks.note: One spray is very effective when applied within two days of infection but repetitive sprays should not be given. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Late Blight - Management (p. 24)

chunks.en: The first symptom of disease is observed as soft tissue necrosis of bark of the stem near soil line. White, cottony and silvery mycelial growth is clearly visible on the affected portion. Later on white to light brown mustard like sclerotium is observed on the same portion.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Symptoms (p. 24)

chunks.en: Progressive dropping and yellowing followed by wilting of the entire plant is observed. Sometime plants collapse soon after infection. The disease is soil borne where pathogen survives in the form of sclerotia.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Symptoms (p. 24)

chunks.en: Use crop rotation with cereals, corn, sorghum and millets. Remove all the weeds from field. Avoid use of infested farmyard manure, soil crop debris and compost in the field.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Management (p. 24)

chunks.en: Irrigate the soil in summer and plough the field to destroy germinating sclerotia. Avoid dense planting and maintain proper aeration near collar region. Use Ammonium Nitrate as a fertilizer for nitrogen source.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Management (p. 24)

chunks.en: Green manuring followed by application of Trichoderma @ 5 kg/ha within a week of ploughing. Seedlings dip in Trichoderma @ 1% for 10 minutes.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Management (p. 24)

chunks.note: Drench near the collar region followed by carbendazim @ 0.1% for immediate control. Fungicide drenching should be done preferably in evening.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Management (p. 24)

chunks.note: Drench near the collar region after Copper Oxychloride @ 0.3% for immediate control. Fungicide drenching should be done preferably in evening.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Collar Rot - Management (p. 24)

chunks.en: Olivacious black sooty growth of fungus was observed on the lower surface of the leaves. Symptoms are only observed on the leaves. Leaf defoliate soon after infection. No discoloration was observed on the corresponding upper side of the leaves.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Pseudocercospora Leaf Blight - Symptoms (p. 24)

chunks.en: Collect and burn the infected leaves. Be careful for selecting exotic hybrids and varieties.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Pseudocercospora Leaf Blight - Management (p. 25)

chunks.note: One spray of hexaconazole or triademefon or bitertanol @ 0.05% at 7-10 days interval.

chunks.en: Infection starts during flowering stage. Soft, wet, water soaked rotting of stem, leaves, fruits, and flowers are observed followed by white fungal growth over it. Fruits are severely affected where sclerotia formed inside and outside of the fruits.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - White Rot - Symptoms (p. 25)

chunks.en: The disease is observed in December to January during low temperature, cloudy weather and high atmospheric humidity accompanied by soil moisture.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - White Rot - Symptoms (p. 25)

chunks.en: Cut the infected plant parts along with some healthy portion in morning and carefully collect in polythene to avoid falling of sclerotia in the field. Burn all these materials away from field.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - White Rot - Management (p. 25)

chunks.note: Foliar spray at flowering stage followed by spray of mancozeb @ 0.25% in cool, cloudy and humid weather.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - White Rot - Management (p. 25)

chunks.note: Spray after the carbendazim @ 0.1% flowering-stage spray, in cool, cloudy and humid weather. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - White Rot - Management (p. 25)

chunks.en: Rhizoctonia fruit rot is most serious disease of kharif tomato. Symptoms appear as rhythmic rotting of fruits coming with the soil contact. Rotting is immediately followed by cracking and fungal growth over it. Generally lower portion of fruits are infected which are coming in soil contact.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Fruit Rots - Symptoms (p. 25)

chunks.en: Avoid the contact of fruit from soil by staking of plant. Provide proper drainage in the field.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Fruit Rots - Management (p. 26)

chunks.en: Green manuring followed by soil application of Trichoderma @ 5 kg/ha in soil is very effective in checking most of the fruit rotting.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Fruit Rots - Management (p. 26)

chunks.en: Small circular dark brown necrotic, numerous spots appear all over the leaf lamina that is uniformly distributed on entire foliage. Sometimes clear narrow yellow halo is visible around the spots. Usually these spots are isolated but in later stage they coalesce to each other. Severely infected older leaves blight and fall down.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Grey Leaf Spot - Symptoms (p. 26)

chunks.en: Periodical monitoring of the crop for initiation of disease from last fortnight of December to first week of January.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Grey Leaf Spot - Management (p. 26)

chunks.note: Foliar spray of either Mancozeb @ 0.25% or Chlorothalonil @ 0.2% two to three times at 7-10 days interval. Restricted use in India: confirm with your KVK or agriculture officer before use.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Grey Leaf Spot - Management (p. 26)

chunks.note: Foliar spray of either Mancozeb @ 0.25% or Chlorothalonil @ 0.2% two to three times at 7-10 days interval.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Grey Leaf Spot - Management (p. 26)

chunks.en: Removal and burning of all crop debris after senescence of the crop.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Grey Leaf Spot - Management (p. 26)

chunks.en: Small, dark spots appear on leaflets and stems of seedlings transplanted crop. Numerous spots coalesce and cause severe burning of the leaves. Prominent yellow halo is observed around the spot.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Spot - Symptoms (p. 26)

chunks.en: Disease appear in rainy season and continued up to fruit initiation stage. The disease in prevalent in warm humid weather when RH is more than 90% and temperature is between 25 and 35 degree C.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Spot - Symptoms (p. 26)

chunks.en: Summer ploughing to desiccate the bacteria and host. Soil solarization in nursery bed to avoid seedling infection. Rotation of nursery seedbed and main field. Seed should be collected from disease free plants.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Spot - Management (p. 27)

chunks.en: Adopt intercropping of urd and mung as mulches to prevent rain splash.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Spot - Management (p. 27)

chunks.en: Use tolerant line of tomato like LE-415.

chunks.en: The spots are necrotic, circular to roughly circular. As the fruit approaches the pink stage, the tissue around the spot retains its green colour longer than normal. Small black spots appear on leaf, petiole, pedicel, and peduncle while irregular, elongated lesions appear on stem.

chunks.en: Bacterial speck is favoured by cool, moist, weather and temperature range between 15 and 25 degree C. Generally, disease is observed in winter season when fruit starts ripening.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Speck - Symptoms (p. 27)

chunks.en: Summer ploughing to desiccate the bacteria and host. Seed should be collected from disease free plants.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Bacterial Speck - Management (p. 27)

chunks.note: Seed dipping in Streptocycline solution @ 100 ppm.

chunks.note: One spray after 10 days of antibiotic application.

chunks.en: Disease appear in severe forms during the month of September to November. Leaves show downward rolling, curling, twisting and chlorosis. chunks.en: Removal of weed host from field near surrounding areas. Nursery should be grown in nylone net to check the white fly infection.

chunks.note: Root dipping for one hour during transplanting of the seedlings.

chunks.en: Seed treatment with hot water at 50 degree C or 10% trisodium phosphate solution for 25 minutes.

chunks.en: Use barrier crop of taller non-host crops like maize, bajra and sorghum. Collect healthy seeds from disease free plants.

chunks.en: Periodical sprays of systemic insecticides up to flower setting. Avoid mechanical injury during intercultural operations. Use tolerant varieties. Roughing of infected plants soon after infection at initial stage of growth.
chunks.locator: Disease management - Tomato - Leaf Curl Complex - Management (p. 28)

chunks.en: Prepare raised nursery beds about 10 cm above ground level for good drainage to avoid damping off.

chunks.en: Cover the beds with polythene sheet of 45 gauge (0.45 mm) thickness for three weeks before sowing for soil solarisation for reducing the soil borne pests. Sufficient moisture should be present in the soil.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - Nursery (p. 57)

chunks.note: Before transplanting dip the roots of seedlings for 15 minutes for management of aphids, white fly & leaf miner.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - Nursery (p. 57)

chunks.en: Transplant a row of marigold after every 16 rows of tomato as a trap crop. Marigold should be 15 days older than tomato plants so that they flower at the same time. Maximum egg laying by borer is observed on marigold flowers. First and last row of plots should be marigold and it should be sprayed with HaNPV.

chunks.en: Adopt wide spacing of 60 x 45 cm (for varieties) and 90x 60 cm (for hybrids) to reduce the chance of spread of diseases.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - (p. 57)

chunks.en: Apply neem cake @ 250 kg/ha at 20 DAP to reduce fruit borer, leaf miner and nematode.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - (p. 57)

chunks.en: Bird perches @ 10/ acre should be erected for facilitating field visits of predatory birds.

chunks.en: Spray of 5% NSKE at 15 DAP has also been found to be effective against leaf-miner & white fly. Spray Imidacloprid or Thiomethoxam at 15 DAP for leaf miner & white fly control, if needed.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - (p. 57)

chunks.en: Pheromone traps @ 5/ ha be installed for monitoring fruit borer activity. Replace the lures with fresh lures after every 20-25 day interval. ETL for fruit borer is 8 to10 moths /day/trap. Monitor top three leaves for Helicoverpa eggs.

chunks.en: Release of T. chilonis, T. braziliensis and T. pretiosum @ 1.0 lakh/ha 4-5 times from flower initiation stage at weekly intervals for fruit borer.
chunks.locator: Recommended IPM practices for important vegetable crops - Tomato - (p. 57)

chunks.en: Showing of resistant variety (Fruit borer-Avinash-2, Bacterial wilt- Arka Abha, Arka Alok, Shakti, Arka Abhijit, Arka Shreshta, Leaf Curl-Parbhani, Yeshree, H.24; Root-knot Nematodes, Hissar Anmol, SL 120, Pusa Hybrid 2; Powdery Mildew- Arka Ashish, Early Blight-Devgiri, Fusarium wilt-Pant Bahar).

chunks.en: Application of well decomposed enriched farmyard manure @ 2 t/ha, enriched with Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2 kg/t of well decomposed FYM against fungal diseases and nematodes.

chunks.en: Soil application of 500 kg of Neem cake against bacterial wilt, serpentine leaf miner and root knot nematodes and 1 tonne of vermin-compost per hectare to the main field before transplanting (induced resistance against biotic stress - pest incidence).

chunks.en: Plastic mulching to reduce pupation in the soil, repels whiteflies in case of silver coloured sheets and also avoids weed growth. Polythene sheets of 25-30 micron thickness (black or silver coloured) should be spread on the raised beds as mulch before transplanting.

chunks.en: Round holes should be made as per the recommended spacing (4 ft x 1.5 ft or 120 cm x 45 cm) using a punch or a large diameter pipe and a hammer and the seedlings should be placed in the holes.

chunks.en: The basic components of AESA are: Plant health at different stages. Built-in compensation abilities of plants. Pest and defender population dynamics. Soil conditions. Climatic factors. Farmers past experience.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, basic components, p.12

chunks.en: Principles of AESA based Integrated Pest Management (IPM): Grow a healthy crop. Select a variety resistant/tolerant to major pests. Treat the seed with recommended pesticides especially biopesticides. Select healthy seeds and seedlings. Follow proper spacing. Soil health improvement (mulching and green manuring). Proper irrigation. Crop rotation.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, principles - grow a healthy crop, p.12-13

chunks.en: Nutrient management especially organic manures and biofertilizers based on the soil test results. If the dosage of nitrogenous fertilizers is too high the crop becomes too succulent and therefore susceptible to insects and diseases. If the dosage is too low, the crop growth is retarded.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, principles - grow a healthy crop, p.13

chunks.en: So, the farmers should apply an adequate for best results. The phosphatic fertilizers should not be applied each and every season as the residual phosphate of the previous season will be available for the current season also.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, principles - grow a healthy crop, p.13

chunks.en: Farmers should: Monitor the field situation at least once a week (soil, water, plants, pests, natural enemies, weather factors etc.). Make decisions based on the field situation and P: D ratio. Take direct action when needed (e.g. collect egg masses, remove infested plants etc.).
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, observe the field regularly, p.13

chunks.en: Understand and conserve defenders: Know defenders/natural enemies to understand their role through regular observations of the agro-ecosystem. Avoid the use of chemical pesticides especially with broad-spectrum activity.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, understand and conserve defenders, p.13-14

chunks.en: Insect zoo concept can be helpful to enhance farmers' skill to identify beneficial and harmful insects. In this method, unfamiliar/unknown predators are collected in plastic containers with brush from the field and brought to a place for study.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, insect zoo, p.14

chunks.en: Each predator is placed inside a plastic bottle together with parts of the plant and some known insect pests. Insects in the bottle are observed for certain time and determined whether the test insect is a pest (feeds on plant) or a predator (feeds on other insects).
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, insect zoo, p.14

chunks.en: Identifying the number of pests and beneficial insects helps the farmers to make appropriate pest management decisions. Sweep net, visual counts etc. can be adopted to arrive at the numbers of pests and defenders. The P: D ratio can vary depending on the feeding potential of natural enemy as well as the type of pest.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, Pest: Defender ratio (P: D ratio), p.14

chunks.en: The natural enemies of tomato pests can be divided into 3 categories 1. parasitoids; 2. predators; and 3. pathogens.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, Pest: Defender ratio (P: D ratio), p.14

chunks.en: The general rule to be adopted for management decisions relying on the P: D ratio is 2: 1. However, some of the parasitoids and predators will be able to control more than 2 pests. Wherever specific P: D ratios are not found, it is safer to adopt the 2: 1, as P: D ratio.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, P: D ratio, p.15

chunks.en: Whenever the P: D ratio is found to be favourable, there is no need for adoption of other management strategies. In cases where the P: D ratio is found to be unfavourable, the farmers can be advised to resort to inundative release of parasitoids/predators depending upon the type of pest.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, P: D ratio, p.15

chunks.en: In addition to inundative release of parasitoids and predators, the usage of microbial biopesticides and biochemical biopesticides such as insect growth regulators, botanicals etc. can be relied upon before resorting to synthetic chemical pesticides.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, A. Agro-ecosystem analysis, P: D ratio, p.15

chunks.en: Go to the field in groups (about 5 farmers per group). Walk across the field and choose 20 plants/acre randomly. Observe keenly each of these plants and record your observations.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Plant: Observe the plant height, number of branches, crop stage, deficiency symptoms etc. Pests: Observe and count pests at different places on the plant. Defenders (natural enemies): Observe and count parasitoids and predators. Diseases: Observe leaves and stems and identify any visible disease symptoms and severity.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Rats: Count number of plants affected by rats. Weeds: Observe weeds in the field and their intensity. Water: Observe the water situation of the field. Weather: Observe the weather condition.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: While walking in the field, manually collect insects in plastic bags. Use a sweep net to collect additional insects. Collect plant parts with disease symptoms. Find a shady place to sit as a group in a small circle for drawing and discussion. If needed, kill the insects with some chloroform (if available) on a piece of cotton.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Each group will first identify the pests, defenders and diseases collected. Each group will then analyze the field situation in detail and present their observations and analysis in a drawing (the AESA drawing).
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Each drawing will show a plant representing the field situation. The weather condition, water level, disease symptoms, etc. will be shown in the drawing. Pest insects will be drawn on one side. Defenders (beneficial insects) will be drawn on another side. Write the number next to each insect. Indicate the plant part where the pests and defenders were found. Try to show the interaction between pests and defenders.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Each group will discuss the situation and make a crop management recommendation. Formulate a common conclusion. The whole group should support the decision on what field management is required in the AESA plot. Make sure that the required activities (based on the decision) will be carried out. Keep the drawing for comparison purpose in the following weeks.
chunks.locator: II. AESA based IPM, AESA methodology, p.17

chunks.en: Ecological engineering for pest management has recently emerged as a paradigm for considering pest management approaches that rely on the use of cultural techniques to effect habitat manipulation and to enhance biological control.

chunks.en: Natural enemies may require 1. Food in the form of pollen and nectar for adult natural enemies. 2. Shelters such as overwintering sites, moderate microclimate, etc are needed. 3. Natural enemies may also require alternate host when primary host are not present.

chunks.en: Ecological engineering for pest management - Above ground: Raising the flowering plants / compatible cash crops along the field border by arranging shorter plants towards main crop and taller plants towards the border to attract natural enemies as well as to avoid immigrating pest population. Growing flowering plants on the internal bunds inside the field.
chunks.locator: III. Ecological engineering for pest management, p.22

chunks.en: Not to uproot weed plants those are growing naturally like Tridax procumbens, Ageratum sp. Alternanthera sp., which act as nectar source for natural enemies. Not to apply broad spectrum chemical pesticides, when the P: D is favourable. The plant compensation ability should also be considered before applying chemical pesticides.
chunks.locator: III. Ecological engineering for pest management, p.22

chunks.en: Ecological engineering for pest management - Below ground: Crop rotations with leguminous plants which enhance nitrogen content. Keeping soils covered year-round with living vegetation and/or crop residue. Adding organic matter in the form of FYM, Vermicompost, crop residue which enhance below ground biodiversity. Reducing tillage intensity so that hibernating natural enemies can be saved.
chunks.locator: III. Ecological engineering for pest management, p.22

chunks.en: Applying balanced dose of nutrients using biobiofertilizers. Apply mychorrhiza and PGPR. chunks.en: Under suitable environmental conditions, the eggs hatch and new larvae emerge to complete the life cycle within 4 to 8 weeks depending on temperature. Nematode development is generally most rapid within an optimal soil temperature range of 70 to 80 degree F.

chunks.en: Infected plants in patches in the field. Formation of galls on host root system is the primary symptom. Roots branch profusely starting from the gall tissue causing a 'beard root' symptom. Infected roots become knobby and knotty.
chunks.locator: VII. Description of insect pests, 6) root-knot nematode, damage symptoms, p.59

chunks.en: In severely infected plants the root system is reduced and the rootlets are almost completely absent. The roots are seriously hampered in their function of uptake and transport of water and nutrients. Plants wilt during the hot part of day, especially under dry conditions and are often stunted.
chunks.locator: VII. Description of insect pests, 6) root-knot nematode, damage symptoms, p.59

chunks.en: Seedlings infected in nursery do not normally survive transplanting and those surviving have reduced flowering and fruit production. Nematode infection predisposes plants to fungal and bacterial root pathogens.

chunks.en: Damping off of tomato occurs in two stages, i.e. the pre-emergence and the post-emergence phase. In the pre-emergence the phase the seedlings are killed just before they reach the soil surface. The young radical and the plumule are killed and there is complete rotting of the seedlings.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 1) damping off, damage symptoms, p.60

chunks.en: The post-emergence phase is characterized by the infection of the young, juvenile tissues of the collar at the ground level. The infected tissues become soft and water soaked. The seedlings topple over or collapse.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 1) damping off, damage symptoms, p.60

chunks.en: Favourable conditions: High humidity, high soil moisture, cloudiness and low temperatures below 24 degree C for few days are ideal for infection and development of disease. Crowded seedlings, dampness due to high rainfall, poor drainage and excess of soil solutes hamper plant growth and increase the pathogenic damping-off.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 1) damping off, favourable conditions, p.61

chunks.en: Survival and spread: Primary: Soil, Seed, Water. Secondary: Conidia through rain splash or wind.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 1) damping off, survival and spread, p.61

chunks.en: Less vigorous plant are usually affected. Small, round to irregular spots with a grey center and dark margin on leaves. Spots usually starts on lower leaves and gradually advance upwards.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 2) Septoria leaf spot, damage symptoms, p.61

chunks.en: Spots coalesce and leaves are blighted. Complete defoliation of affected leaves. Stems and flowers are sometimes attacked. Fruits are rarely attacked.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 2) Septoria leaf spot, damage symptoms, p.61

chunks.en: Survival and spread: Primary: Mycelium or conidia in pycnidia in infected plant debris or on solanaceous weeds. Secondary: Conidia through rain splash or wind and also by slimy conidia sticking on to hands and clothing of tomato pickers.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 2) Septoria leaf spot, survival and spread, p.62

chunks.en: Favourable conditions: Poor vigour of plants due to nutrient inadequacy or in late season. High humidity or persistent dew at 25 degree C. Moist weather with intermittent showers.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 2) Septoria leaf spot, favourable conditions, p.62

chunks.en: Disease appears as spots on leaves, stems and fruits and as wilting of leaves and shoots. White blister like spots in the margins of leaves. Spots become brown with age and coalesce, but leaves do not fall off. Leaflets on one side of rachis show withering initially.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 3) bacterial stem and fruit canker, damage symptoms, p.62

chunks.en: Light coloured streaks on stems and petioles at the joints. Cracks develop in streaks and form cankers. Slimy bacterial ooze through the cracks in humid weather.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 3) bacterial stem and fruit canker, damage symptoms, p.62

chunks.en: Small, shallow, water soaked, spots with white halo develop on fruits. The centers of spots become slightly raised, tan coloured and rough. Vascular discolouration is seen in split open stems.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 3) bacterial stem and fruit canker, damage symptoms, p.62

chunks.en: Survival and spread: Primary: Bacterial cells survive on infected plant debris and seed (both internally and externally) and also on solanaceous weeds such as Solanum nigrum. Secondary: Bacterial cells transmitted through rain splash.

chunks.en: Favourable conditions: Soil temperature of around 28 degree C. High humidity or persistent dew. Moist weather with intermittent showers.

chunks.en: This is a common disease of tomato occurring on the foliage at any stage of the growth. The fungus attacks the foliage causing characteristic leaf spots and blight. Early blight is first observed on the plants as small, black lesions mostly on the older foliage.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 4) early blight, damage symptoms, p.63

chunks.en: Spots enlarge, and by the time they are one-fourth inch in diameter or larger, concentric rings in a bull's eye pattern can be seen in the center of the diseased area. Tissue surrounding the spots may turn yellow. If high temperature and humidity occur at this time, much of the foliage is killed.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 4) early blight, damage symptoms, p.63

chunks.en: Lesions on the stems are similar to those on leaves, sometimes girdling the plant if they occur near the soil line. Transplants showing infection by the late blight fungus often die when set in the field.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 4) early blight, damage symptoms, p.63

chunks.en: The fungus also infects the fruit, generally through the calyx or stem attachment. Lesions attain considerable size, usually involving nearly the entire fruit; concentric rings are also present on the fruit.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 4) early blight, damage symptoms, p.63

chunks.en: Survival and spread: Primary: The fungus spends the winter in infected plant debris in or on the soil where it can survive at least one and perhaps several years. It can also be seed borne.
chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 4) early blight, survival and spread, p.63

chunks.en: Secondary: The spores are transported by water, wind, insects, other animals including man, and machinery. Once the initial infections have occurred, they become the most important source of new spore production and are responsible for rapid disease spread.

chunks.en: Favourable conditions: Warm, rainy and wet weather.

chunks.en: Moist weather and splattering rains are conducive to disease development. Most outbreaks of the disease can be traced back to heavy rainstorms that occur in the area. chunks.en: The most striking symptoms are on the green fruit. Small, water-soaked spots first appear which later become raised and enlarge until they are one-eighth to one-fourth inch in diameter. chunks.en: Characteristic symptoms of bacterial wilt are the rapid and complete wilting of normal grown up plants. Lower leaves may drop before wilting. chunks.en: Infected plant parts when cut and immersed in clear water, a white streak of bacterial ooze is seen coming out from cut ends.

chunks.locator: VIII. Description of diseases, 7) leaf curl, damage symptoms, p.65

chunks.en: Older leaves become leathery and brittle. The nodes and internodes are significantly reduced in size. The infected plants look pale and produce more lateral branches giving a bushy appearance. The infected plants remain stunted.

chunks.en: The leaflets of affected leaves are usually distorted, puckered and smaller than normal. Sometimes the leaflets become indented resulting in "fern leaf" symptoms. The affected plant appears stunted, pale green and spindly.

chunks.en: Symptoms vary among hosts and in a single host species. Stunting is a common symptom of TSWV infection. Chlorotic or necrotic rings form on the leaves of many infected hosts. chunks.en: Affected plants may have a one sided growth habit or may be entirely stunted and have drooping leaves, suggesting a wilt. Pale red or yellow areas with concentric circular marking in the normal red skin of ripe tomato are formed. Discoloration of seed.
